Package org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic

Class AgenticToolEndRecorder

java.lang.Object
org.cibseven.connect.ai.agent.agentic.AgenticToolEndRecorder
All Implemented Interfaces:
DelegateListener<DelegateExecution>, ExecutionListener
public class AgenticToolEndRecorder extends Object implements ExecutionListener
Records on a tool's performance which interrupting boundary event interrupted its flow: on the tool itself, or on an activity further along its chain (CIB7-2166). The scope's observer takes it into the entry the agent is told about, and a tool result into what the call returns.

Without it, the agent learnt only where the flow ended, endedAt; a tool whose error path ran to its end within the call was even reported as finished.

Set by the parse listener in two places, the start of a boundary event and the end of the activity it is attached to, and does three things, told apart by the activity, the event it is notified of and how that activity ended:

  • the start of an interrupting boundary event that is no error event: records it;
  • the end of an activity a boundary error event is attached to, as the error cancels it: records the error with the code AgenticCaughtError caught. Here, not at the event's start, because that end runs in the command that caught the error, also when the event itself continues asynchronously;
  • the end of every activity a boundary event is attached to, when it completes, not cancelled and not ended by a BPMN error nothing caught, which the engine ends it with as if it had completed: forgets what that activity's events recorded earlier in the same performance. An event's path led back to it, and this time it did its work. Only that repairs an interruption: a flow that goes back to before the interrupted activity and ends without completing it again still reports it, and a retry that is still running does too.

Built in, so skipCustomListeners does not skip it.
